answer.diagnosis: The shortcut is a small 3x3 patch in the top-left corner (image rows 1-3, columns 1-3), far from the central blob. About 18 of the 32 first-layer units carry very large weights there (|w| of roughly 40-99), much larger than their other weights. Units 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20 and 29 have strongly positive weights on the patch. Units 5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27 and 30 have strongly negative weights on it. Each of these units also has a ring or disc pattern over the image centre, which is the genuine size feature. The near-random noise units (3, 7, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, 19, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28, 31) show no such patch. A tightly localised corner block, outside where the blob sits and shared across many units with opposite signs, points to a corner marker that was correlated with the label during training. The fix zeroes these corner-patch weights in every first-layer unit. The central size detectors are left unchanged. One residual effect: the patch weights no longer pick up background noise in that corner, so unit activations may shift slightly. I did not compensate in the biases because the background level is unknown.
